recommendation_1: Replace the single linear layer with a two-layer feedforward network by modifying the Net class to use nn.Sequential with hidden layers: nn.Linear(784, 128) followed by nn.ReLU() and then another nn.Linear(128, 10). This allows the model to learn more complex representations than a simple linear classifier.
rationale_1: A single linear layer cannot capture non-linear relationships in the data. Adding one hidden layer with ReLU activation enables the model to learn hierarchical feature representations, which is essential for image classification tasks like MNIST.
recommendation_2: Add dropout regularization by inserting nn.Dropout(0.2) after the first fully connected layer in the modified Net class. Specifically, change the sequential layers to include dropout: nn.Linear(784, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.2), nn.Linear(128, 10).
rationale_2: Dropout prevents overfitting by randomly setting a fraction of input units to zero during training. With a small amount of dropout (0.2), it helps generalize better, especially important when dealing with non-IID data distributions across clients.
recommendation_3: Change the activation function from ReLU to Swish (SiLU) by importing torch.nn.SiLU and replacing nn.ReLU() with SiLU() in the modified Net class. This provides smoother gradients and may improve convergence speed.
rationale_3: Swish activation has been shown to outperform ReLU in many cases due to its smoothness and self-gating property, which allows for better gradient flow and can lead to improved model performance without increasing complexity significantly.
recommendation_4: Use a convolutional neural network instead of a fully connected network by defining a new Net class with CNN layers: nn.Conv2d(1, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2), nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(32*14*14, 10).
rationale_4: CNNs are specifically designed for image data and can automatically extract spatial hierarchies of features. Given that MNIST images have spatial structure, a CNN will likely perform much better than a flat fully connected network.
recommendation_5: Modify the optimizer to use AdamW with weight decay instead of SGD by changing optimizer initialization to: torch.optim.AdamW(net.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=1e-4).
rationale_5: AdamW combines adaptive learning rates with decoupled weight decay, which generally leads to faster convergence and better generalization compared to standard SGD with momentum, particularly useful in FL settings with heterogeneous data.
